summary: Igor Dmitrievich Serebryakov (1917–1998) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Saint Petersburg State University (ca. 1936–1940). He held posts at Pravda, the Military Institute of Foreign Languages, and the Institute of Oriental Studies (ca. 1960–1998).

Ihsan Ali is a historian and archaeologist who studied at the University of Peshawar and under Frank Raymond Allchin. His career includes serving as Professor at Peshawar, Director of Archaeology and Museums in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, and Vice Chancellor of Hazara University.
Ikko Arai is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Komazawa University. Arai studied under Shiro Matsumoto, Kazunobu Matsuda, Lambert Schmithausen, Harunaga Isaacson, and Michael Zimmermann.

Ikuhisa Takigawa is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied at Waseda University. In 2002, he was attested as a part-time lecturer (非常勤講師) at both Waseda University and Tokai University.

Ikuko Tazaki is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. In 2017, Tazaki was attested as a special researcher at the Shin Buddhist Comprehensive Research Institute and a collaborative researcher at Kyoto University.

Ilkka Pyysiäinen is a religious studies and philosophy scholar who studied under René Gothóni and earned a PhD at the University of Helsinki. He served as an Academy Research Fellow at Helsinki and a visiting researcher at the University of Oxford.

Immanuel Kant (1724–1804) was a philosopher who studied at Collegium Fridericianum and the University of Königsberg (1740–1746). He held the chair of logic and metaphysics at the University of Königsberg from 1770 and taught Johann Gottfried von Herder.

Imre Galambos works in Sinology, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Eötvös Loránd, Nankai, and UC Berkeley. His posts include the British Library, UC Santa Barbara, Zhejiang University, and the University of Cambridge.

Imre Hamar is a Sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Eötvös Loránd University, National Taiwan Normal University, and under Noritoshi Aramaki. He became a Professor at Eötvös Loránd University in 2006 and a visiting professor at Otani University.

In-gun Kang is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. Kang completed an STL at Santa Clara, an MA at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, and a doctorate at Heythrop College under Michael Barnes.

Ines Konczak-Nagel is a scholar of archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Central Asian studies. She has held posts as a visiting research fellow at Ryukoku University (2012) and as a postdoctoral research fellow at the Berlin State Museums.

Ingmar Heise works in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA in Chinese Studies at Leiden University (completed by 2005) and was attested as a PhD candidate at the University of Bristol in 2012.

Ingo Strauch is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed a PhD at the Free University of Berlin in 2000. He taught Kathrin Holz and was attested as a professor at the University of Lausanne in 2018.
Inyoung Chung is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Virginia (attested 2008), where the doctoral supervisor was Paul Groner.

Ioan Petru Culianu (1950–1991) was a scholar of religious studies and history who studied at Bucharest, Catholic University of the Sacred Heart, and Paris-Sorbonne, alongside Mircea Eliade. He held posts at the University of Groningen and Chicago Divinity School.

Irawati Karve (1905–1970) was an Indology and archaeology scholar who studied at Huzurpaga, Fergusson College, and the University of Mumbai under Govind Sadashiv Ghurye. She later held a post at the University of Pennsylvania (ca. 1951–1952).

Irfan Habib is an Indian historian and Indologist who studied at Minto Circle, Aligarh Muslim University, and New College, Oxford. He served as a historian at Aligarh Muslim University from around 1953 to 1991.

Irving Babbitt (1865–1933) was a philosopher who studied at Williams College, the University of Paris, and Harvard University. He taught Yongtong Tang and held faculty posts at Williams College (ca. 1892–1893) and Harvard University (ca. 1894–1933).

Isaac Schapera (1905–2003) studied at Cándido Candi, the University of Cape Town, and the London School of Economics. He taught Bridget Allchin and held academic posts at Chicago, Toronto, and the London School of Economics (ca. 1950–1969).

Isaak Jakob Schmidt (1779–1847) was a scholar in Tibetology, Central Asian, and Buddhist studies who received a doctorate from Rostock (1825). He served as treasurer for the Russian Bible Society and held memberships at the Imperial Academy of Sciences.
